questions.q: Which invoice line type represents the actual goods or services being billed?
options: Freight
Item
Miscellaneous
Withholding Tax
questions.explain: Item lines carry the core content of the invoice — the goods or services themselves.

questions.q: What does 'Allocate All Lines' do with a freight charge?
options: Deletes the freight line entirely
Converts the freight line into a credit memo
Spreads the freight charge proportionally across the existing item lines, using their account combinations
Moves the freight charge to a separate invoice
questions.explain: Allocation spreads a freight or miscellaneous charge across item lines automatically, avoiding manual account coding.

options: A supplier's bank account detail
A type of payment term
A business classification certificate
The breakdown of an invoice line into the specific GL account(s) and amounts it posts to
questions.explain: A distribution is the actual accounting result of a line — which account(s) it posts to and how much.

questions.q: Can a single invoice line produce more than one distribution?
options: Yes, for example when a line's amount is split across two departments' accounts
No, it is always exactly one distribution per line
Only for Miscellaneous lines
Only when the invoice type is Mixed
questions.explain: A line can be split into multiple distributions, such as a percentage split across two expense accounts.

questions.q: What must be true about the sum of an invoice's distributions?
options: They can total anything; it doesn't matter
They must always equal exactly one distribution
They must sum back to the invoice's total line amount, which must match the header amount
They only need to match if the invoice is PO-matched
questions.explain: Distribution totals must tie back to the invoice amount; a mismatch is one of the holds validation can raise.
